ask.text:
Once a year the village holds a teaching day, when every elder takes on one young person and teaches them everything they can in a single day. This year, (subject) has been paired with (young), who has never shown the slightest interest in anything (subject) does.
(young) is sitting cross-legged, arms folded, already bored. (subject) can teach (subject.him/her) the hard way, properly, from the beginning, or try to find whatever (young) actually cares about and teach that.
How should (subject) teach?

c1o1.text: By the afternoon (young) has stopped yawning and started asking questions, and by evening (young.he/she) is arguing with (subject) about the right way to do it, and is occasionally right. The skills aren't the ones (subject) set out to teach, exactly: (young) has just learned how to learn. Whatever (young.he/she) was already good at, (young.he/she) gets better at, fast.

c1o2.text: (subject) is such a good teacher, it turns out, that by noon other young people have drifted over to listen, and by afternoon there's a crowd. Three of them go home with their heads full and their hands itching to try. (young), who started all this, is sulking at the back. "I was here first," (young.he/she) says.

c1.text: (subject) starts at the beginning, the way (subject.he/she) was taught: slowly, carefully, every step explained twice. (young) yawns. Then, despite (subject.himself/herself), (young.he/she) starts to watch...

c2o1.text: So (subject) takes (young) to watch birds, and talks about how the birds build their nests, and how that is exactly how a roof is built, or a basket woven, or a net tied. By the end of the day, (young) has decided that tying thatch is just bird-work with bigger hands, and the splinters of rough wood, which (young.he/she) always hated, don't bother (young.him/her) anymore.

c2o2.text: (subject) talks about birds all day: their feathers, their calls, their eggs, which ones are good to eat. By sunset (young) has heard more about birds than anyone ever should. (young.He/She) never looks at a bird the same way again. "You ruined birds," (young.he/she) tells (subject), and (subject) has to admit (subject.he/she) might have overdone it. After a whole day of it, (young) has no appetite for lessons of any kind.

c2.text: "What do you like?" (subject) asks. (young) shrugs. "Nothing." (subject) waits. Eventually, sullenly, (young) admits to liking watching the birds...
